prompt:
Several teams filed reports about people who were removed from a workspace.

1. Security: a contractor was removed from the members page two weeks ago. Yesterday they posted a comment in that workspace from a browser tab they still had open, and they can switch into the workspace from the workspace picker of another account they hold. The members page does not list them.
2. Support: a designer who had left was invited back. She accepted the new invitation and saw a "you are a member" confirmation, but the workspace never appeared in her list and opening it says she is not a member. Sending another invitation gives the same result every time.
3. Notifications: people who left keep getting emails and in-app notifications: when someone comments on an issue they opened, when an issue assigned to them becomes overdue, and one of them still receives the daily digest.
4. Project management: issues can still be assigned to people who have left, new projects can be created with a former member as lead, and existing projects keep showing a former member as their lead.
5. Admin: an admin working from a stale tab changed the role of someone who had already been removed, and the audit log now shows a role change for a person who is not in the workspace. Removing that person a second time from the same tab also reported success, and the seat count dropped again.

Expected behaviour. From the moment a member is removed they are a former member for every purpose. They cannot act in the workspace or switch into it, even with a session that was valid before. They are not notified about anything that happens afterwards, whatever the kind of notification, they are not a digest recipient, and mentions of them in comments are ignored. Work cannot be assigned to them and they cannot be a project's lead; the same goes for anyone who is not a current member of the workspace, and such a change is refused as a whole, with nothing created or changed. The issues assigned to them become unassigned and the projects they led have no lead. Changing their role or removing them again is refused as a conflict, exactly as archiving something already archived is, and frees no further seat. Their memberships in other workspaces are untouched.

A former member can be invited back. Accepting the invitation re-admits them as the member the workspace already knew: the same membership, with whatever was recorded about it before they left still attached, now active, with the role and the inviter named on the invitation and the acceptance time as their join date, listed once, taking one seat, and notified again from then on. An invitation is used up by being accepted, whoever accepts it: when a current member accepts one, nothing about them changes (not their role, not the seats), but the invitation can no longer be used.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Root cause (shared membership contract, repository layer): the member repository has two notions of "gone" (status = suspended vs archived_at) and every consumer reads a different one. Injected (bug.patch, 1 file, 2 defects): (a) findMember lost its live-row predicate (comment: the row's status says whether it is usable); (b) archiveMember no longer sets status = suspended (comment: status records what the membership was). Together a removed member still resolves to an Actor (session-service resolveActorForOrg, member-service resolveActor, switchActiveOrg), and acceptInvitation's "already a member" short-circuit finds the archived row and returns it, so a re-invited person never gets back in. Latent in the pristine corpus and exercised by the prompt: the notification fan-out (notify) and the digest recipient list address anyone named, member or not; issue create/assign and project create/update accept any user id as assignee/lead; removal leaves stale assignee/lead references; role change and second removal on an archived membership succeed (findMemberById ignores archive) and emit events (the second removal decrements the seat counter again through the usage listener); re-joining via a fresh invitation would hit the members_org_user_idx UNIQUE index if inserted. Reference fix (10 files, 3 layers, ~256 changed lines): types/member isActiveMembership; member-repository findMember live-only again, archiveMember sets suspended, findMembership (archived included, re-join only), isActiveMember, filterActiveMemberIds, reactivateMember (same row: status active, archived_at null, invitation role/inviter, fresh joinedAt); issue-repository unassignIssuesForUser; project-repository clearLeadForUser; member-service assertNotArchived on role change/removal, cascade unassign + clear lead on removal, exported assertActiveMember (NotFoundError); issue-service and project-service validate assignee/lead before writing; notification-service notify filters recipients to active members; digest-service filters digest recipients; invitation-service acceptInvitation reactivates an archived membership, consumes the invitation even for an already-active member and emits member.joined only for a (re)join. Traps: fixing only the status column leaves re-join returning the archived row; fixing only the read predicate makes re-join crash on the UNIQUE index; delete-then-insert on re-join changes the member id, which the test pins (the audit trail must stay attached, as the repository's own comment says); emitting member.joined for an already-active acceptor double-counts the seat; findMemberById must keep returning archived rows or the conflict cannot be raised. SqliteError UNIQUE on re-join; naive C (complete except re-join = delete old row + insert) 1/18 fail; hidden x3 stable.
